findings.title: totalPages counts one page too many when user_count is an exact multiple of limit.
findings.body: `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` gives 2 pages for 50 members with limit 50, and 3 pages for 100. On the real last page `showingLast` is false, so "next" stays enabled. Clicking it sets `offset = min(offset+limit, user_count) = user_count`, which loads an empty page and shows e.g. "2/2" with no members. Use `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)` instead.

findings.title: Public group members page now shows only the first 50 members and has no way to page.
findings.body: `findMembers` now asks for `limit: 50`, and the server now paginates every group, not just automatic ones. This template lists `members` but has no next/previous controls, unlike the admin page. Any group with more than 50 members now shows a truncated list on the public page, which is a regression from the old full list. Add pagination or load-more controls here as well.

findings.title: Public members endpoint accepts any client-supplied limit/offset with no bounds.
findings.body: Any user who can see the group can call `/groups/:name/members.json?limit=10000000` and get every member serialized in one response. A negative `limit` or `offset` makes Postgres raise "LIMIT/OFFSET must not be negative", which returns a 500. Before this change only automatic groups were paginated, and the default was 200. Clamp `limit` to a sane maximum such as 1..200 and set `offset` to at least 0.

findings.title: Add-members input is never cleared, so adding twice re-adds existing members.
findings.body: The TODO admits the usernames field keeps its value after a successful add. If the admin clicks "Add" again, or adds a username that is already in the group, `add_members` calls `group.add(user)` for a user who is already a member. With a uniqueness validation on GroupUser, `<<` raises, so the request fails with a 500. The client ignores the error, so nothing tells the admin it failed. Clear `usernames` after success, add a failure handler, and skip existing members on the server.

held.title: Removing a member through `group.users.delete(id)` skips the model's removal logic and errors on non-members.
held.body: The old code used `group.remove(user)`. `users.delete` on a has_many :through deletes the join rows directly, so GroupUser destroy callbacks do not run. Anything those callbacks maintain, such as the cached user_count or a user's primary group or title, may become stale; I could not check the model to confirm which callbacks exist. Also, a `user_id` that is not in the group makes `delete` call `find`, which raises RecordNotFound. Use `group.remove(User.find(user_id))`, or destroy the GroupUser record.
